signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Tightening + Positioning Extreme
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1198 following hotter-than-expected US September CPI at 3.7% year-over-year against 3.6% consensus. The Fed policy rate at 4.00% versus the ECB at 2.65% maintains a 135bp nominal carry advantage for the dollar, reinforced by a +145bp OIS SOFR-over-ESTR spread. CFTC data shows institutional leveraged funds hold EUR net short of -84,775 contracts at the 4th percentile of the 52-week range (z = -1.64), reflecting acute institutional short crowding. Technically, EUR/USD holds well below its SMA20 at 1.1312, SMA50 at 1.1484, and SMA200 at 1.1595, cementing entrenched downside momentum. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; macro carry differential and policy repricing dominate despite stretched spec shorts. Catalyst: Eurozone CPI release at 09:00 UTC today. Risk: Eurozone headline inflation beats sharply above 2.9% and triggers short-covering toward 1.1312.

signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard flags a major weekly divergence with NOK averaging +0.792% across 2 pairs against EUR declining -0.271% across 9 pairs, generating a 1.063% bilateral spread. Norges Bank maintains its policy rate at 4.50% with an active hiking bias, while the ECB sits at 2.65% with a hold bias, establishing a +185bp nominal carry premium favoring the krone. Energy price resilience with WTI holding at $94.8 sustains Norwegian terms-of-trade outperformance while broader European growth lags. BEER fair-value modeling indicates EUR/NOK is stretched at -2.76 standard deviations below fair value, yet fundamental rate divergence continues to drive capital into Scandinavian yields. Trade bias: Long NOK/EUR; wide policy rate wedge and terms-of-trade favor continued outperformance. Catalyst: ECB meeting 29 Oct — hold priced. Risk: Sharp crude oil liquidation below $90 invalidates the terms-of-trade advantage.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.90, holding above its SMA20 at 157.75 and SMA50 at 157.72 while capped immediately below its SMA200 at 158.49. A 275bp policy rate advantage of Fed 4.00% over BoJ 1.25% and a +266bp SOFR-TONA carry spread sustain broad dollar demand. However, the 1-month 25-delta risk reversal sits at -1.70, signaling heavy options market demand for downside put protection. Implied volatility trades at 7.6% against a 30-day realized volatility of 9.5%, creating an inverted volatility risk premium of -1.9% that highlights underpriced realized swings. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; wide rate differential supports the pair while remaining below the 160.00 intervention threshold. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct — hold priced. Risk: Sustained break below the SMA50 at 157.72 accelerates downside options delta hedging.

signals.title: USD/CAD — COT vs Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4212, positioned comfortably above its SMA20 at 1.4170, SMA50 at 1.3990, and SMA200 at 1.3871. A wide policy differential of Fed 4.00% versus BoC 2.25% creates a +175bp dollar carry cushion, reinforced by a +161bp OIS spread. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds heavily net short CAD at -82,720 contracts (21.2% long ratio), while retail sentiment sits at an extreme 95% net short USD/CAD. This severe institutional versus retail divergence establishes capitulation squeeze risk for retail traders as spot pushes multi-month highs. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; institutional trend and rate differential override contrarian retail positioning. Catalyst: BoC meeting 28 Oct — hold priced. Risk: Sustained price drop below the SMA20 anchor at 1.4170.
